rapport_notes: Friendly, warm tone; good pace and conversational style; genuine engagement with customer's preferences.
process_discipline_notes: No detected repetitions or silence-holding violations on the calls that occurred.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "the reason I'm calling we received your quote request earlier today and I wanted to touch base with you gather some more details" — no time-boxed framing or promise of accuracy; jumps to logistics.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into confirming address, packing, move size without probing for customer's concerns or priorities.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns raised by customer during discovery, so no follow-up required. Customer is compliant and logistics-focused.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "usually, usually for a house the size, we would need two trucks, four movers for about six to eight hours" — gives range and size reference, but doesn't personalize to the specific customer's floor count, walk distance, or other mentioned factors.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: "we'll just prorate the time in every fifteen minutes instruments. In that way, you only pay for the actual time that it" — references 15-minute increment logic; credits partial hit on this line.
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock mention. No explicit ask. Call ends with "I will give you two pricing" and handoff to walkthrough link; clean routing but no formal close.

top_strength: Excellent routing discipline and clean handoff: rep correctly identified a 2200 sq ft move, recommended virtual walkthrough, offered multiple upload methods (afternoon video call, email link, photos), and confirmed next steps without abandoning the pitch.
coaching_note: Front-load the agenda question ("Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?") before diving into logistics confirmation — this would surface any hidden concerns and create a real discovery conversation, not just a data-collection call.
